title: Influence of osteopathic intervention on pain symptoms and the autonomic nervous system of patients with craniomandibular dysfunction (CMD)
summary:
In this study, people with pain caused by teeth grinding are treated individually with osteopathic manual medicine three times within a month for approx. 30 minutes in addition to standard physiotherapeutic and orthodontic treatment. It is assumed that the pain will remain significantly less than with standard treatment even after two further months.  
Whether the treatments are associated with changes in the autonomic nervous system is checked using heart rate variability parameters.

This study takes place in a medical practice. The heart rate variability measurement and the questionnaires will be collected by a person who does not know which treatment has taken place.

interventions.name: Standard physiotherapeutic/orthodontic treatment of CMD: over one month at two-week intervals, i.e. three sessions of 30 minutes each
Standard physiotherapeutic/orthodontic treatment of CMD and additional osteopathic manual therapy (OMT): over one month at two-week intervals, i.e. three sessions of 30 minutes each

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- adults aged 18 and over 
- (Dental) medical CMD diagnosis (ICD-10: K07.6)
- Study-relevant complaints for at least three months
Exclusion criteria:
- Wearing a pacemaker or atrial fibrillation (queried as part of the medical history)
- higher-grade cardiac arrhythmia
